sections.title: From compound to certification
sections.live: LIVE H2 → From Compound to Certification · six steps · “compression moulding” is right on this page

fields.label: Steps
rows: Material compounding — polymer blending, additive integration and batch QC in our in-house lab. The FKM grade and cure system are set here, against your medium.
Mould design and CNC tool manufacture, in-house, held as a controlled record. Tooling is compound-specific — FKM, silicone and NBR shrink differently, so one part in three compounds is not one tool.
Compression moulding — [no change; correct on this part]

Post-cure — FKM is oven post-cured to complete crosslinking and drive off cure by-products. Without it the compound does not reach its published temperature or compression-set performance. The step that makes the +250 °C real.
Quality inspection — dimensional check, hardness, and compression set on batch samples to ASTM D395 Method B.

Export packaging — industrial packing with documentation. ISPM-15 treated pallets where timber packaging is used. Inlays are packed uncompressed, since an insert stored under load arrives already set.
fields.note:
Six steps, six kept — the process is right and four steps gain the detail that makes it specific.
Step 04 is the one that matters on an FKM page. Post-curing is real, non-obvious and cost-bearing, and a supplier who skips it ships FKM that does not perform as FKM — a genuine failure mode in this trade.
Step 02 carries the commercial fact that explains why the minimum run is per compound rather than per part

notes: The process block must render from the part record — right here by luck, not by data.

fields.label: Credit, an addition, and two cautions
paragraphs: ISO 9001:2015 claimed and nothing else — no IATF, no TÜV SÜD, no CE marking. The production table prints “On request” rather than inventing figures, and the video says “Film pending”. The scope covers a moulded insert, so the badge stands unqualified.
